mainTopic: אדמון and the חכמים on whether a later deal disproves an earlier debt, רב נחמן and רב ששת on two mutual loan documents, and the three lands of ארץ ישראל for marriage.
overview: This amud brings two משניות where אדמון and the חכמים argue. In the first, a lender later sold a field to his borrower. In the second, two people each hold a שטר חוב against the other. אדמון says the later deal proves the first debt was not real. The חכמים say the first document still stands. The גמרא explains the field case: the argument is only where the document is written before the money is paid, and it turns on whether the lender should have made a מודעא. For the two documents, רב נחמן says each one collects, and רב ששת says swapping is pointless. Their argument is explained as a question of how land quality is ranked: by each owner's own fields, or by one standard for everyone. The גמרא then tries several ways to fit the משנה with רב ששת. These include loans of different lengths and cases involving orphans. Finally, a new משנה teaches that ארץ ישראל counts as three separate lands for marriage.

steps.title: The case of the field sale and אדמון's argument
steps.stepSummary: A lender shows a שטר חוב, and the borrower shows that the lender later sold him a field. אדמון says the borrower can argue that the sale proves he owed nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone shows a loan document against his friend. The friend answers by showing that the lender sold him a field. אדמון says the borrower can argue: 'If I really owed you, you would have collected your money when you sold me the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה presents a case and gives אדמון's opinion that the later sale weakens the lender's claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sale document is dated after the loan. אדמון's logic is simple: a person who is owed money takes it back from the borrower instead of selling him a field. So the sale suggests the debt was already paid or never existed.

keyTerms.meaning: A judge in ירושלים whose rulings are recorded in this פרק
To collect payment of a debt

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who produces a promissory note against his fellow,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַלָּה הוֹצִיא שֶׁמָּכַר לוֹ אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה.
phrases.english: and the other produced [a document] that he sold him the field.
phrases.notes: The borrower brings a bill of sale, dated after the loan, showing that the lender sold him a field.

phrases.english: Admon says: He can say:
If I had owed you,
you should have collected what is yours
when you sold me the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹצִיא שְׁטַר חוֹב עַל חֲבֵרוֹ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אדמון, a later sale from the lender to the borrower lets the borrower argue that no debt existed.

steps.title: The חכמים say the lender was clever
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject אדמון's proof. The lender may have sold the field on purpose so that he could seize it as collateral for the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: This lender was smart. He sold him the land because now he can take it as collateral.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give the opposing view in the משנה: the sale does not disprove the loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the field belongs to the borrower, the lender can collect it for the debt. So the sale could have been a strategy to secure his loan, not a sign that there was no loan.

keyTerms.meaning: To take it as collateral (a pledge)

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
This one was clever,
in that he sold him the land
because he can take it as collateral from him.
phrases.notes: Now that the field is in the borrower's hands, the lender can grab it for the debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: זֶה הָיָה פִּקֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes אדמון's ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sale does not cancel the loan document, because the lender may have sold the field in order to seize it.
steps.whatToRemember: אדמון: the sale proves there was no debt. חכמים: the sale was a smart move to have something to collect from.

steps.title: The גמרא asks why the רבנן disagree with אדמון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finds אדמון's argument convincing and asks what the reasoning of the רבנן is.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason of the רבנן? אדמון is saying something good!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן because אדמון's logic seems very strong. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender received money from the borrower when he sold the field. He could simply have kept that money as payment of the debt. So why would anyone sell a field to a person who owes him money?

keyTerms.meaning: He is saying well, his point is good

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason of the Rabbis?
Admon is speaking well!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן? שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר אַדְמוֹן
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lender received money during the sale and could have kept it as payment, so אדמון's argument seems correct.

steps.title: Where money is paid first, everyone agrees with אדמון
steps.stepSummary: In a place where people pay first and write the bill of sale afterward, all agree that the borrower's argument works.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a place where people give the money first and then write the document, everyone agrees the borrower can say: 'You should have collected your debt when you sold me the field.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by narrowing the dispute. In one kind of place, the רבנן fully agree with אדמון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the money is handed over first, the lender could simply have kept it as repayment and refused to write the sale. Since he didn't, the borrower's argument is strong.

keyTerms.meaning: In a place, meaning a place with a certain local custom

phrases.english: In a place where they give the money
and afterward write the document,
everyone agrees
that he can say to him:
You should have collected what is yours
when you sold me the field.
phrases.notes: The money was already in the lender's hand, so he could have just kept it as payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַתְרָא דְּיָהֲבִי זוּזֵי וַהֲדַר כָּתְבִי שְׁטָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question by limiting where the רבנן argue.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the dispute to a specific local custom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן reject אדמון's argument in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where payment comes before the document, the רבנן agree with אדמון.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the רבנן always reject אדמון. In a pay-first place they agree with him completely.

steps.title: Where the document comes first, אדמון says a מודעא was needed
steps.stepSummary: The real dispute is in a place where the bill of sale is written before payment. אדמון holds that the lender should have made a protest declaration.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue in a place where people write the document first and pay afterward. אדמון holds: the lender should have handed over a declaration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the exact case of the dispute and explains אדמון's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the document is written first, the lender is already committed to the sale and can't simply keep the money as repayment. Even so, אדמון says that if the lender meant to sell only so he could seize the field, he should have told witnesses so ahead of time. Without that declaration, the sale counts against him.

keyTerms.meaning: A declaration made before witnesses ahead of time, stating one's true intention

phrases.english: Where they disagree
is in a place where they write the document
and afterward give the money.
Admon holds:
He should have handed over a declaration.
phrases.notes: He should have told witnesses beforehand that he was selling only so he could later seize the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, בְּאַתְרָא דְּכָתְבִי שְׁטָרָא וַהֲדַר יָהֲבִי זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case where all agree to the case where they argue.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Locating the dispute and giving each side's reasoning
steps.terutzMaskana: In a write-first place, אדמון requires a מודעא to keep the debt alive.

steps.title: The רבנן: a מודעא would have leaked out
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain why the lender did not make a declaration: word would have spread and reached the borrower.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: Your friend has a friend, and your friend's friend has a friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by giving the reasoning of the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender had told witnesses about his plan, the news would have passed from person to person until the borrower heard it. Then the borrower would have backed out of buying the field. So the lack of a מודעא proves nothing.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:
Your friend has a friend
and your friend's friend has a friend.
phrases.notes: In other words, the secret would have spread until the borrower heard it and called off the deal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: חַבְרָךְ חַבְרָא אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's side of the dispute set up in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why no declaration was made
steps.terutzMaskana: The lender could not safely make a מודעא, so its absence does not weaken his loan document.
steps.whatToRemember: Pay-first place: everyone agrees with אדמון. Write-first place: אדמון says the lender should have made a מודעא, and the רבנן say a מודעא would have leaked out.

steps.title: Two people each holding a loan document against the other: אדמון's view
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: two people each produce a שטר חוב against the other. אדמון says the later borrower can argue: 'Why would you borrow from me if I owed you?'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Two people each showed a loan document against the other. אדמון says: 'If I owed you, how could you be borrowing from me?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second case with the same kind of reasoning: a later deal suggests the earlier debt was not real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the field sale, the second loan seems to contradict the first. Someone who is owed money would collect it, not borrow from his debtor. So אדמון treats the earlier document as suspect.

keyTerms.meaning: One against the other, each against the other

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Two people who produced
a promissory note, each against the other,
Admon says:
If I owed you,
how is it that you are borrowing from me?!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ שְׁטַר חוֹב זֶה עַל זֶה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אדמון, a later loan from the creditor to his debtor undermines the earlier loan document.

steps.title: The חכמים: each one collects his own loan
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים rule that both documents are valid, so each person collects what is written in his own document.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: This one collects his loan document, and that one collects his loan document.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with אדמון and treat both loan documents as valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the second loan does not cancel or disprove the first. Each document stands on its own, and each holder collects his debt.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
This one collects his promissory note,
and that one collects his promissory note.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: זֶה גּוֹבֶה שְׁטַר חוֹבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes אדמון's ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both loan documents are valid, and each holder collects his own debt.
steps.whatToRemember: In both משניות, אדמון says a later deal proves the earlier debt was fake. The חכמים say the earlier document still stands.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about two mutual loan documents
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that each holder of a שטר חוב collects from the other. רב ששת says swapping is pointless, so each keeps what he has.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: two people each produced a loan document against the other. רב נחמן said: this one collects and that one collects. רב ששת said: why should I bother swapping loads back and forth? Rather, each one stays with what he has.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an argument between later Sages about the case in the משנה, where two people each hold a loan document against the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים in the משנה said both documents are valid. Now רב נחמן and רב ששת argue about what that means in practice. רב נחמן says there is a real two-way collection. רב ששת says that if the debts are equal, collecting back and forth changes nothing, so each simply keeps his own.

keyTerms.meaning: Shifting the loads (on a donkey) from side to side. It means a pointless exchange.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ שְׁטַר חוֹב זֶה עַל זֶה.
phrases.english: Two people who produced a loan document, each against the other.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: זֶה גּוֹבֶה וְזֶה גּוֹבֶה.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: this one collects and that one collects.
Rav Sheshet said:
Why do I need to shift the loads back and forth?
phrases.notes: Picture moving a donkey's packs from one side to the other. It's the same load either way, so nothing changes.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא זֶה עוֹמֵד בְּשֶׁלּוֹ וְזֶה עוֹמֵד בְּשֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: Rather, this one stays with his own, and that one stays with his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ שְׁטַר חוֹב זֶה עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's ruling (Step 8) that both documents are valid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: each one collects. רב ששת: each keeps his own, because swapping is pointless.

steps.title: Where both sides agree: land of equal quality
steps.stepSummary: If both men's land is of the same quality, everyone agrees that collecting back and forth is pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees: if it is best land against best land, middle against middle, or worst against worst, it is certainly just a pointless swap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to pin down the exact argument. It first shows the case where רב נחמן and רב ששת agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land is ranked in three levels: עידית (best), בינונית (middle), and זיבורית (worst). If both men would be collecting land of the same level, nobody gains anything from swapping. So even רב נחמן agrees with רב ששת here. This sets up the next step, where they really disagree.

phrases.english: Everyone agrees:
best land against best land,
middle land against middle land,
worst land against worst land:
it is certainly just shifting loads back and forth.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא עִידִּית וְעִידִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the argument in Step 9 by showing the case where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both men's land is of equal quality, everyone agrees there is no swap.

steps.title: Where they argue: middle-quality land against worst land
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about a case where one man has בינונית and the other has זיבורית. רב נחמן holds that each owner's land is ranked against his own fields.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they argue is where one has middle land and the other has worst land. רב נחמן holds that each one collects, because he holds that land is assessed by the owner's own fields.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now names the exact case where רב נחמן and רב ששת disagree. It also gives רב נחמן's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two men own land of different quality, so swapping may not be pointless. רב נחמן's key idea is בשלו הן שמין: whether a field counts as best, middle, or worst depends on the other fields that same person owns. So the same field could be 'middle' for one man and 'best' for another.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (introduces the reason for a view).
Land quality is assessed by comparing the owner's own fields.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think of 'best' and 'middle' as fixed labels for a field. According to רב נחמן, the label depends on what else that owner has.

phrases.english: Where they disagree
is where one has middle-quality land
and the other has worst land.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן סָבַר: זֶה גּוֹבֶה וְזֶה גּוֹבֶה.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman holds: this one collects and that one collects.
He holds: they assess by his own land.
phrases.notes: 'His own' means we rank a field by comparing it to the other fields this same person owns.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, דְּאִית לֵיהּ לְחַד בֵּינוֹנִית וּלְחַד זִיבּוּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 10 showed where they agree, this step shows where they argue and gives רב נחמן's reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a case of בינונית against זיבורית, רב נחמן says each collects, because land is ranked against the owner's own fields.

steps.title: How the two collections come out different
steps.stepSummary: The man with worst land collects the other's middle land. For him it now counts as best, so the second man ends up collecting his worst land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner of the worst land comes and collects the middle land from the other. For him, that field now counts as best land. Then the other man comes and takes the worst land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out step by step how רב נחמן's rule plays out. It shows why the two collections are not just a pointless swap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A creditor normally collects from the borrower's middle land, so the man with only worst land takes the other's בינונית. That field is better than anything else he owns, so it now counts for him as his best land. When the second man collects in return, the field he takes is his debtor's 'worst' land. So the two men end up exchanging different fields, and the collection is meaningful.
steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן and רב ששת agree that equal-quality land means no swap. They argue only when the land differs. רב נחמן says each collects because land is ranked against the owner's own fields, so the two collections give different results.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב נחמן's 'each collects' is not a contradiction of common sense. Once fields are ranked per owner, a real difference appears between the two collections.

phrases.english: The owner of worst land comes
and collects the middle-quality land,
which becomes, for him, best land,
phrases.notes: Compared with his other fields, which are all worst land, this field is now his best.

phrases.english: and that other one comes and takes worst land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָתֵי בַּעַל זִיבּוּרִית וְגָבֵי לֵיהּ לְבֵינוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the practical result of רב נחמן's reason (בשלו הן שמין) from Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רב נחמן's view, the man with worst land takes the other's middle land, which becomes his best. The other man then collects the worst land, so the exchange is real.

steps.title: Why רב ששת says swapping is pointless
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת holds that land quality is measured by a general standard, so the second man simply takes back his own middle field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת, who said 'Why should we flip the packs back and forth?', holds that land quality is judged by a standard that applies to everyone. So in the end, when the second man comes to collect, he just takes back his own middle-quality field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב ששת's ruling from step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן ranked each man's land against his own fields. רב ששת uses one general scale for everyone. On that scale the middle field stays 'middle' no matter who holds it, so the second man collects that same field right back. Nothing has really changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'flipping the packs'. It means pointless shifting back and forth.
He holds (introduces the reasoning behind someone's view)
Land is judged by a general standard that applies to everyone

phrases.english: And רב ששת, who said:
Why do I need to flip the packs back and forth?
phrases.notes: This is his line from step 9. It is a saying about moving the same load back and forth for no reason.

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: בְּשֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם הֵן שָׁמִין,
phrases.english: holds: they judge land by the standard of all people,
so ultimately, when that other one comes to collect,
he is just taking back his own middle-quality land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר הַפּוֹכֵי מַטְרָתָא לָמָּה לִי קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the dispute by giving רב ששת's side, right after steps 11 and 12 gave רב נחמן's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב ששת, land quality is judged by a general standard, so the second creditor just recovers his own middle field and the exchange accomplishes nothing.

steps.title: Why assume the worst-land owner collects first?
steps.stepSummary: Against רב נחמן: if the middle-land owner collected first, the same field would just go back and forth.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב נחמן, why do you assume the owner of the worst land comes first? Let the owner of the middle land come first and collect the worst land. Then the other man will go back and collect that same field from him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation of רב נחמן's view. It asks why the order of collecting is assumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 worked only because the זיבורית owner collected first. Reverse the order: the בינונית owner takes the זיבורית field, and then the זיבורית owner collects that same field right back. That swap is pointless, so רב נחמן's ruling seems to depend on a random choice of order.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why choose this option over the other?)

phrases.english: And according to רב נחמן:
what did you see
that makes the owner of the worst land come first?
Let the owner of the middle land come first
and collect the worst land,
and then let the other go back and collect it from him!
phrases.notes: The worst-land owner just takes his own field back, so nothing changes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב נַחְמָן מַאי חָזֵית דְּאָתֵי בַּעַל זִיבּוּרִית בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case description in step 12, which explained רב נחמן's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in step 12 that the זיבורית owner collects first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing forces that order. With the opposite order, the same field goes back and forth even according to רב נחמן, so the explanation of the dispute does not hold.

steps.title: He claimed first
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the worst-land owner happened to file his claim first.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed only where the worst-land owner claimed first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying the order is fixed: the זיבורית owner made his claim first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the זיבורית owner sued first, he collects first. That locks in the order from step 12, so רב נחמן's back-and-forth exchange produces a real result.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (limits a ruling to a specific case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
where he went ahead and claimed from him first.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דִּקְדֵים תַּבְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order of collection seemed random, which would make רב נחמן's exchange pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The זיבורית owner claimed first, so he collects first.

steps.title: They collect at the same time
steps.stepSummary: The answer is rejected: even if one claimed first, both come to collect together.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the end, when they come to collect, they come together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each man holds a שטר against the other, so the court handles both debts together. Who filed first does not set the order of collection. The order problem from step 14 comes back.

phrases.english: But ultimately, when they come to collect,
they come together!

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף כִּי אֲתוֹ לְמִגְבֵּי בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי קָאָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that claiming first fixes the order of collection.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both debts are collected together, so who claimed first makes no difference.

steps.title: The real case: one owns best and middle land, the other only worst
steps.stepSummary: The argument is moved to a case where one man owns עידית and בינונית and the other owns only זיבורית. רב נחמן ranks by each man's own land; רב ששת ranks by a general standard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the argument is needed where one man has best land and middle land, and the other man has only worst land. One master (רב נחמן) holds that land is ranked against the owner's own fields. The other master (רב ששת) holds that it is ranked by a general standard for everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the earlier case, the גמרא gives a new case. Here the two views really give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case changes so the order of collection no longer matters. According to רב נחמן, the זיבורית owner comes out ahead: he collects the other man's middle land and pays back with worst land. According to רב ששת, land is ranked by one general scale, so the same field just goes back and forth.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)
Land is ranked against the owner's own fields

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: rank by each man's own land (בְּשֶׁלּוֹ). רב ששת: rank by a general standard (בְּשֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם). The argument makes a real difference when one man has עידית and בינונית and the other has only זיבורית.
steps.confusionAlert: This new case replaces the earlier one (one man with בינונית, the other with זיבורית). Do not mix the two cases together.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the whole argument is about one question: how do we rank land quality? Each man's own fields, or one standard for everyone? That question decides what a creditor may collect.

phrases.english: Rather, it is needed
where one man has best land and middle land,
and the other man has worst land.
One master holds: they rank it against his own land,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: בְּשֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם הֵן שָׁמִין.
phrases.english: and one master holds: they rank it by the standard of all people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָא צְרִיכָא דְּאִית לֵיהּ לְחַד עִידִּית וּבֵינוֹנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected case with a new one that answers the question from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New case setting (אוקימתא) that replaces the earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about one man with בינונית and the other with זיבורית, but there the result depended on who collected first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about one man with עידית and בינונית and the other with only זיבורית. The views differ on whether land is ranked by the owner's own fields or by a general standard.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן ranks land by each owner's own fields, so the זיבורית owner gains. רב ששת ranks land by a general standard, so the exchange is pointless.

steps.title: The משנה's ruling seems to clash with רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in the משנה, who say both men collect, as a challenge to רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: the חכמים say, this one collects and that one collects!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the words of the חכמים in the משנה as a challenge to רב ששת. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים rule that each man collects his own debt from the other. רב ששת said that collecting back and forth is pointless, so each keeps what he has. The משנה seems to say the opposite, so רב ששת needs an answer.

phrases.english: We learned: And the Sages say:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about אדמון, where two men each hold a loan document against the other.

phrases.english: This one collects and that one collects!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: זֶה גּוֹבֶה וְזֶה גּוֹבֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's position, which was set out in steps 13 and 17.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules plainly that both collect, which seems not to match רב ששת's approach.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains the משנה as loans of different lengths
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains the משנה in a way that fits רב ששת: one loan was for ten years and the other for five.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן explained it according to רב ששת: for example, where this one borrowed for ten years and that one for five.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends רב ששת by placing the משנה in a special case where the two loans have different due dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the loans come due at different times, it makes sense that each man collects on his own document. The משנה is not about two equal debts canceling out, so it does not contradict רב ששת.

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב נַחְמָן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman explained it according to Rav Sheshet:
For example, where this one borrowed for ten (years)
and that one for five.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב נַחְמָן אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the משנה to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about two equal debts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about loans with different time periods, ten years and five years.

steps.title: The first loan cannot be the ten-year loan
steps.stepSummary: If the first loan were for ten years and the second for five, אדמון would have no argument, because the first debt was not yet due.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say the first loan was for ten years and the second for five, would אדמון really say in this case, 'If I owed you, how could you borrow from me?' But the due date had not come yet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact details of רב נחמן's case and rules out one possible version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדמון's argument is: 'If I really owed you, you would have asked me for your money instead of borrowing from me.' But if the first loan was for ten years, it was not due yet. So of course the man had to borrow, and אדמון's argument makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (what are the exact details)
אדמון, the תנא who argues with the חכמים in the משנה

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say the first (loan) was for ten and the second for five,
would Admon say in this case:
phrases.notes: This is said with surprise: אדמון would never make his argument in this case.

phrases.english: If I owed you,
how is it that you borrow from me?
But its due date had not arrived!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא רִאשׁוֹן לְעֶשֶׂר וְשֵׁנִי לְחָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible reading of the case in step 19 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the version where the first loan was for ten years.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that version the first debt was not yet due, so אדמון's argument would not work.

steps.title: The first loan was for five years, the second for ten
steps.stepSummary: So the case must be that the first loan was for five years and the second for ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the first loan was for five years and the second for ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles on the other version of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the first debt comes due sooner, so אדמון can argue that the man should have asked for his money back instead of borrowing. This version gives אדמון a real argument.

phrases.english: Rather, the first was for five,
and the second for ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רִאשׁוֹן לְחָמֵשׁ, וְשֵׁנִי לְעֶשֶׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the version that was rejected in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the details of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the first loan was for ten years.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first loan was for five years and the second for ten.

steps.title: Was the five-year loan already due or not?
steps.stepSummary: Either way there is a problem. If the five years were over, why do the חכמים let both collect? If not, what is אדמון's argument?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If its due date had arrived, what is the reason of the חכמים? And if its due date had not arrived, then it simply was not due yet, so what is the reason of אדמון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new version of the case with a 'heads or tails' problem: each option makes one side of the argument hard to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the five-year debt was already due, the man should have collected it instead of borrowing, so the חכמים seem wrong. If it was not due yet, he had no choice but to borrow, so אדמון seems wrong. Neither option explains why there is an argument at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If this... and if that (two options)
The Sages (the חכמים of the משנה)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If its due date had arrived,
what is the reason of the Rabbis?
And if its due date had not arrived,
then it simply had not arrived,
phrases.notes: In other words, of course he borrowed, since he could not demand the money yet.

phrases.english: so what is the reason of Admon?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דִּמְטָא זִמְנֵיהּ — מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case that was settled on in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a five-year first loan and a ten-year second loan
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided problem: if the loan was due, the חכמים are hard to explain; if it was not due, אדמון is hard to explain.

steps.title: He borrowed on the exact day the five years ended
steps.stepSummary: The case is when the second loan was taken on the very day the five-year loan came due. They argue whether a person would borrow just for one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he came on the very day the five years were completed. One Sage holds a person does borrow for one day, and the other Sage holds a person does not borrow for one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the two-sided problem by finding a case right in the middle: the very day the first debt became due.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On that day the money was due, but he could only get it at the end of the day. The חכמים say a person might still borrow to cover that one day, so his borrowing proves nothing. אדמון says nobody borrows for just one day; he would have waited, so his borrowing shows the other man never really owed him.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (this specific case)
One Sage holds... and the other Sage holds
A person does (this kind of thing)

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between אדמון and the חכמים, as explained here for רב ששת, comes down to one question about how people behave: would someone take a loan just to cover a single day?
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר' is the חכמים (a person does borrow for one day), and the second 'מר' is אדמון (a person does not). Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary where he came
on that very day when the five (years) were completed.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: עֲבִיד אִינִישׁ דְּיָזֵיף לְיוֹמֵיהּ,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: a person will borrow for a day,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: לָא עֲבִיד אִינִישׁ דְּיָזֵיף לְיוֹמֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: a person will not borrow for a day.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא דַּאֲתָא בְּהָהוּא יוֹמָא דְּמִשְׁלַם חָמֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two-sided challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pinpointing a middle case and finding the real point of disagreement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The loan was either clearly due or clearly not due.
steps.terutzMaskana: It became due on that same day, and the argument is whether people borrow for one day.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: the case involves orphans
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא explains that one of the two borrowers died, so his orphans can collect what is owed to them, but no one can collect from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: Here we are dealing with orphans. Orphans can collect debts owed to their father, but we do not let others collect from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא offers a new way to understand the משנה. He says one of the two people died, and his orphans are now involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another way to defend רב ששת against the משנה from step 18. Normally, equal debts collected both ways would just be shifting loads. But if one side is orphans, who can collect and cannot be collected from, then 'each collects' has a real effect: only the orphans actually get paid.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans (the heirs of the borrower who died)
We do not let others collect (from them)

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama said:
Here we are dealing with orphans,
for orphans do collect [debts owed to their father],
but we do not make them pay [their father's debts].

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר: הָכָא בְּיַתְמֵי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge against רב ששת in step 18. רב נחמן answered with loans of different lengths (steps 19–23); רמי בר חמא instead sets the משנה in a case involving orphans.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (one side is orphans)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'this one collects and that one collects' seemed to contradict רב ששת, who says equal mutual debts are just shifting loads.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the orphans actually collect, so the ruling has a real effect.

steps.title: But the משנה says both collect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רמי בר חמא: the משנה clearly says 'this one collects and that one collects.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: 'This one collects and that one collects'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רמי בר חמא's explanation using the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רמי בר חמא, only the orphans really collect. But the משנה's wording says both sides collect, which does not fit his explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: This one collects and that one collects

phrases.english: But it teaches: "this one collects and that one collects"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא זֶה גּוֹבֶה וְזֶה גּוֹבֶה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 24 from the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's explanation that only the orphans collect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says both sides collect, but in his case only one side does.

steps.title: One collects, the other has the right but nothing to take
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה means one side actually collects, and the other has the right to collect but has nothing to collect from.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one collects, and that one is entitled to collect but has nothing to collect from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רמי בר חמא by reading the משנה's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second 'collects' is read as 'has the right to collect' instead of 'actually collects.' The other creditor has a valid claim, but the orphans have no land he can take.

keyTerms.meaning: But he has nothing (to collect from)

phrases.english: This one collects,
and that one is entitled to collect but has nothing [to collect from].

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה גּוֹבֶה, וְזֶה רָאוּי לִגְבּוֹת וְאֵין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by reinterpreting the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second 'collects' only means he has the right to collect.

steps.title: רבא's first objection: the wording says both collect
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he has two objections to רמי בר חמא. The first: the משנה really does say that both actually collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There are two objections to this. One: the משנה teaches 'this one collects and that one collects.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins rejecting רמי בר חמא's explanation. He announces two objections and gives the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not accept the reading of step 26. In his view, 'this one collects and that one collects' plainly means both sides actually get paid, not that one side merely has a right on paper.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two objections to this

phrases.english: Rava said:
There are two objections to this matter.

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא: דְּזֶה גּוֹבֶה וְזֶה גּוֹבֶה קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: One: that it teaches "this one collects and that one collects."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁתֵּי תְּשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 26 and reopens the wording problem.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רמי בר חמא's whole explanation, beginning with the wording
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plain wording says both actually collect.

steps.title: רבא's second objection: pay the orphans with land, then take it back
steps.stepSummary: רבא's second objection: the other creditor can pay the orphans with land and then collect that same land back from them, as רב נחמן taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, let him pay the orphans with land and then go back and collect it from them, like רב נחמן. For רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Orphans who collected land for their father's debt, a creditor can come back and collect it from them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his second objection, backed up by a ruling of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the orphans had no land at first, once they collect land from the living creditor, that land can be taken back for their father's debt. So in the end the two debts cancel out anyway, and רמי בר חמא's case does not solve the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him pay them with land
And go back and collect it (from them)
A creditor (the one who lent money)
A debt owed to their father

steps.whyThisMatters: רב נחמן's rule shows that land the orphans collect becomes available to their father's creditors.

phrases.english: And furthermore, let him pay the orphans with land
and then go back and collect it from them,
in line with Rav Nachman.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: For Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
Orphans who collected land for a debt owed to their father,

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל חוֹב חוֹזֵר וְגוֹבֶה אוֹתָהּ מֵהֶן.
phrases.english: a creditor can come back and collect it from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, לַגְבִּינְהוּ אַרְעָא לְיַתְמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second of רבא's two objections announced in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that orphans can collect without being collected from
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Land the orphans collect can be taken back by their father's creditor, so the debts still cancel out.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's explanation stands refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רבא's objections are a real difficulty for רמי בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this round and admits that רמי בר חמא's explanation has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The single word 'קשיא' means the objection stands and no answer is given, so this explanation is set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a difficulty (the objection stands)

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the branch opened in step 24 by accepting רבא's objections.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רמי בר חמא's orphan explanation is rejected.

steps.title: Why not explain it as a case of different land quality?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another case: the orphans have only poor land and the other man has good and middle land, so the orphans collect middle land but pay with poor land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us explain the משנה as a case where the orphans have poor land, and he has good and middle land. The orphans collect middle land from him and pay him with poor land. For even if land quality is judged by everyone's land, still, one collects from orphans' property only from poor land!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we don't explain the משנה with a different case, where the 'each one collects' ruling would make a real difference because of land quality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A creditor normally collects middle land, but from orphans he collects only poor land. So if the orphans collect middle land from him while he collects only poor land from them, each side collecting changes the outcome, and the חכמים's ruling has a point.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us set it up (explain the case as)

phrases.english: But let us set it up where the orphans have poor-quality land,
and he himself has best-quality and middle-quality land,
so the orphans go and collect middle-quality land,
and pay him with poor-quality land.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי נָמֵי בְּשֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם הֵן שָׁמִין,
phrases.english: For even if they judge [land quality] by everyone's land,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין נִפְרָעִין מִנִּכְסֵי יְתוֹמִים אֶלָּא מִזִּיבּוּרִית!
phrases.english: still, one collects from orphans' property only from poor-quality land!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ דְּאִית לְהוּ לְיַתְמֵי זִיבּוּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the orphan explanation failed, proposes a different orphan case based on land quality.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that no orphan case can explain the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Different land quality rules for orphans would make 'each one collects' meaningful.

steps.title: A creditor who already took land keeps it
steps.stepSummary: The rule that orphans pay with poor land applies only before the creditor has taken anything. Once he has seized land, he keeps it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only where he has not seized land. But where he has seized, he has seized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the land-quality suggestion of step 30 by limiting the 'poor land' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the creditor already holds middle land, the land the orphans would want to collect from him. Since he has already seized it, he keeps it for his debt, so again nothing changes by having each side collect.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only in this case)

steps.whatToRemember: Every attempt to explain the משנה with orphans has failed. A creditor who already holds land keeps it, even against orphans.
steps.confusionAlert: 'תפס' does not mean he grabbed something new now. It means he is already holding the land, so it stays with him.

phrases.english: This applies only where he has not seized [land],
but where he has seized,
he has seized [and keeps it].

steps.title: The three lands of ארץ ישראל for marriage
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that יהודה, עבר הירדן, and הגליל count as three separate lands for marriage. A husband may not move his wife from one land to another, but he may move her within the same land.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are three lands for marriage: יהודה, עבר הירדן, and הגליל. A husband may not take his wife out of one land to a town or city in another land. But inside the same land, he may move her from town to town or from city to city.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out where a husband may and may not make his wife move inside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats ארץ ישראל as three separate regions for this law. Crossing from one region to another counts as taking her away from her land, so he cannot force it. Moving inside the same region is allowed, whether between small towns or between big cities.

keyTerms.meaning: The land on the other (eastern) side of the Jordan River
Take out, meaning making the wife move
A large city, as opposed to an עִיר, a smaller town

steps.whatToRemember: For moving a wife, ארץ ישראל counts as three lands. He cannot force her to move between them, but he can move her within one of them.
steps.confusionAlert: The first half does not forbid all moves from town to town. It forbids only moving her from a town in one land to a town in a different land. Moving within the same land is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule that the rest of the משנה and the גמרא will build on: where a husband may make his wife live.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל is divided into three lands for marriage. A husband may not force his wife to move from one land to another, but he may move her between towns or cities within the same land.
